name: Gold Scholarship (Gold Scholars Program)
value: Georgia residents: Tuition, Fees, and Books scholarship (valued about $12,500 annually). Out-of-state students: Tuition Waiver (valued about $21,000 annually; reduces cost to the in-state rate). Up to eight semesters of funding, plus retreats, mentoring and first-year housing priority.
deadline: Apply for admission by the Early Action deadline. Georgia Tech 2026-2027 dates: Early Action 1 (Georgia students) October 15; Early Action 2 (non-Georgia students, including international) November 2; Regular Decision January 6.
apply: No separate application. Apply for first-year admission by the Early Action deadline; selection is based solely on the admission application (essays and activities), in the same process as Stamps President's Scholars.
eligibility: First-year applicants (not transfers) who are citizens or permanent residents of the United States or the United Kingdom; citizens of the Republic of Ireland may also be considered. Offered to roughly the top two percent of the first-year class.
notes: Must compete in and keep the primary major listed on the application until the end of the first spring term, or the scholarship is revoked. EA1 date shown is for Georgia students; non-Georgia students use EA2 (November 2).

name: College of Engineering Dean's Scholars Program
value: $10,000 each academic year for up to 8 semesters, plus $2,000 for academic enrichment
deadline: No separate deadline stated; selection is from incoming engineering first-year students. Georgia Tech 2026-2027 dates: Early Action 1 (Georgia students) October 15; Early Action 2 (non-Georgia students, including international) November 2; Regular Decision January 6.
apply: No application process is described; a reading committee and program administrators identify 7 to 20 incoming first-year engineering students each fall. Contact the program director for details.
eligibility: Incoming first-year undergraduates admitted to College of Engineering majors with exemplary academic achievement in high school and strong community service experience.
notes: Cohort size depends on available philanthropic funding.

name: Scheller College of Business Dean's Scholarship (incoming first-year)
value: Four-year scholarships ranging from $20,000 up to $50,000 during an undergraduate career; about 15 to 18 awarded each year
deadline: No separate scholarship deadline stated. Georgia Tech 2026-2027 dates: Early Action 1 (Georgia students) October 15; Early Action 2 (non-Georgia students, including international) November 2; Regular Decision January 6.
apply: The page gives no separate application; apply for first-year admission as a Business Administration student.
eligibility: High school students applying to enter the Georgia Tech summer or fall first-year class as Business Administration students, selected for academic performance, leadership, involvement and potential for success.
notes: Recipients are expected to engage in the Business Administration community.

name: Dickinson Merit Scholarships and Academic Awards
value: $15,000 to $45,000 per year, renewable for eight semesters
deadline: Considered with the admission application. Early Decision I and Early Action: November 15; Early Decision II and Regular Decision: January 15.
apply: No additional application materials required; the admissions committee awards merit scholarships during application review.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students with exemplary academic performance and potential contribution to the college, without regard to financial need.
notes: Renewal requires full-time enrollment and good academic standing (the grants page cites a 2.0 GPA). A separate Dickinson page describes a John Dickinson Scholarship of $20,000 per year renewable with a 3.0 GPA.

name: Reynolds Leadership Scholar Program
value: $50,000 per year toward tuition, $200,000 over eight semesters, plus leadership programming and mentoring
deadline: Reynolds Scholarship application due with the admission application: November 15 (Early Decision I and Early Action) or January 15 (Early Decision II and Regular Decision), per the fall 2027 application form.
apply: Submit the Dickinson application (Common App or Coalition) plus the separate Reynolds Scholarship application with essays on entrepreneurial pursuits and community leadership.
eligibility: Maryland residents and/or students currently enrolled in a Maryland high school who show outstanding leadership, academic excellence and community impact.
notes: Keep with a 2.0 GPA and full-time enrollment.

name: Dickinson-Sandia Scholarship
value: Two full-tuition scholarships, for eight semesters of full-time study
deadline: Complete application plus FAFSA and CSS Profile by the admission application deadline (Early Decision I/Early Action November 15; Early Decision II/Regular Decision January 15).
apply: No separate application. Submit a complete admission application plus the FAFSA and CSS Profile by the deadline; Early Decision applicants get preference.
eligibility: Incoming students who live or attend school in Arizona, New Mexico or Southern California (Imperial, Kern, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo and Ventura counties) with community-service or community-leadership experience.
notes: Only available at the time of admission. The page asks for FAFSA and CSS Profile but does not say need is a selection factor.

name: Curley Scholarship
value: Two half-tuition scholarships awarded annually, for eight semesters of full-time study
deadline: Complete application plus FAFSA and CSS Profile by the admission application deadline (Early Decision I/Early Action November 15; Early Decision II/Regular Decision January 15).
apply: No separate application. Submit a complete admission application plus the FAFSA and CSS Profile by the deadline; Early Decision applicants get preference.
eligibility: Incoming students who live or attend school in Lycoming, Lehigh or Northampton counties, Pennsylvania.
notes: Consideration is based on residency; only available at the time of admission.

name: Music Scholars Award
value: Covers one full credit of private studio lessons each semester (up to $1,500 annually or $6,000 over four years)
deadline: No separate deadline stated; submit materials with the admission application.
apply: Submit supplemental music materials (performance, composition, or academic work in music) through SlideRoom via the Common Application.
eligibility: Prospective first-year students with musical talent; recipients do not need to major in music.
notes: Must join a faculty-led ensemble (Choir, Jazz Ensemble or Orchestra) and take lessons or a music course each semester.

name: Gettysburg Academic Merit Scholarships
value: $30,000 to $53,000 annually, renewable for up to eight semesters
deadline: No separate deadline; considered with the Common Application.
apply: Submit the Common Application; no separate scholarship application.
eligibility: All first-year applicants are considered, based on academic achievement, leadership and potential to contribute to the campus community.
notes: Renewal requires meeting the associated GPA requirement.

name: Eisenhower Scholarship for Civic Engagement
value: $53,000 per year ($212,000 over four years of full-time study)
deadline: Early Decision I by November 1; Early Action by November 15; Regular Decision by January 15; Early Decision II by January 20. ED and EA applicants get priority consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application and the Fall 2027 Eisenhower Scholarship application (two 300 to 350 word essays on civic engagement).
eligibility: First-year applicants with demonstrated civic engagement, leadership and change agency in their communities.
notes: Keep with a 3.0 GPA. Non-recipients are automatically considered for other academic merit scholarships.

name: Gettysburg College-Gilder Lehrman Institute (GLI) History Scholarship
value: $50,000 per year ($200,000 over four years); a limited number awarded each year
deadline: Early Decision I: November 1; Early Action: November 15; Regular Decision: January 15; Early Decision II: January 20. ED and EA applicants get priority consideration.
apply: Submit the Common Application and the GLI Scholarship application with a supplemental essay.
eligibility: High-achieving first-year applicants with a strong interest in history shown through academics, independent research or personal experience.
notes: The fall 2027 GLI application form was not found online yet; the prior-year form is closed. Non-recipients are automatically considered for other merit scholarships.

name: Sunderman Conservatory of Music Scholarships
value: F. William Sunderman Scholarship: $52,000 per year (music majors). Parker B. Wagnild Scholarship: $44,000 per year (music majors or minors). Elizabeth Headley Paul '64 Memorial Scholarship: up to $8,000 per year (keyboard/piano preference).
deadline: 2026-27 audition dates: November 9, 2026; December 12, 2026; January 23, 2027; February 6, 2027. Recorded auditions due November 7 (ED1), December 12 (EA), January 23 (ED2), February 6 (RD).
apply: Complete the Common Application and the Music Profile Form, then schedule an in-person or recorded audition.
eligibility: First-year applicants pursuing a music major or minor at Gettysburg; audition required.
notes: Renewable with satisfactory progress in the music degree, private study and GPA. The Patrick Grant is need-based and not included here.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: $5,000 to $40,000 per year, with larger awards to the strongest students; automatically renewed for four years of full-time study
deadline: Priority Application Deadline for Scholarship Consideration: December 1. Early Decision I: November 15; Early Decision II and Regular Decision: January 15.
apply: No separate application; first-year applicants are automatically considered during admission review.
eligibility: First-year and transfer applicants with outstanding academic and personal achievements.
notes: Union says its merit scholarships are open to international students, with preference to binding Early Decision applicants.

name: Henle Scholarship
value: Amount not stated; automatically renewed for four years of full-time study
deadline: Priority Application Deadline for Scholarship Consideration: December 1.
apply: No separate application is described; awarded to selected incoming first-year students.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students with a unique combination of outstanding talents and accomplishments, academic excellence, and promise of exceptional contribution to the College community.
notes: Established by David L. Henle '75.

name: John F. Oberlin Scholarship
value: Amount not stated; renewable for 8 semesters (10 for Double Degree or BA+BFA students)
deadline: No separate deadline; awarded through admission review.
apply: No separate application; admitted College of Arts and Sciences students are reviewed automatically.
eligibility: Admitted students in the College of Arts and Sciences, based on academic achievement.
notes: Full-time enrollment required. Separate from Oberlin's $10,000 Commitment Scholarship, which goes to every enrolling student.

name: Conservatory Dean's Award
value: Amount not stated; renewable for 8 semesters (10 for Double Degree students)
deadline: Fall 2027 Conservatory deadlines: Early Decision Common App November 1, audition/interview request and screening materials November 4; Regular Decision Common App December 1, request and screening materials December 4, final audition recordings February 1. Music Theater Early Decision: October 15.
apply: Apply to the Conservatory and audition; the Conservatory Admissions Office awards scholarships automatically based on audition ratings and ensemble needs.
eligibility: Admitted Conservatory of Music students.
notes: Oberlin says nearly all admitted conservatory and double-degree students received merit scholarships in 2025-26.

name: Oberlin College National Merit Scholarship
value: $2,000 (Oberlin's policies page states $1,000 to $2,000)
deadline: Follows the National Merit Scholarship Program timeline; list Oberlin as first-choice college with NMSC.
apply: Apply to Oberlin and declare Oberlin as your first-choice college with the National Merit Scholarship Corporation.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists who name Oberlin as first choice and have not won another National Merit or corporate-sponsored National Merit Scholarship.

name: USD First-Year Merit Scholarships
value: Amounts not stated on the official pages; renewable for up to four years (four and a half for Engineering students)
deadline: No separate deadline; considered with the admission application. USD first-year deadlines: Early Decision I and Early Action November 1; Early Decision II January 5; Regular Decision January 15.
apply: No separate application; all first-year applicants are considered automatically.
eligibility: All undergraduate first-year applicants to the University of San Diego (private, in San Diego; not UC San Diego), via holistic review of grades, course rigor, leadership, service, talent and personal qualities.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.0 cumulative USD GPA.

name: USD Music Scholarship and Choral Scholars Scholarship
value: USD Music Scholarship: $540 to $15,000. Choral Scholars Scholarship: $1,200 to $10,000.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; the Music Department says dates and more info for spring 2027 are coming soon.
apply: Audition with the Department of Music (Choral Scholars: two contrasting memorized selections, no longer than five minutes).
eligibility: USD Music Scholarship: incoming or continuing music majors who excel in performance, composition, education or music research. Choral Scholars: music majors or comprehensive minors.
notes: Choral Scholars requires annual re-audition and a minimum 3.0 GPA.

name: First-Year Merit Scholarships
value: Amounts vary; can be as high as $42,000 per year, applied to tuition only, for eight semesters.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No separate application; admitted first-year applicants who apply by the deadline are automatically considered.
eligibility: New first-year applicants to Chapman. Awards are need-blind and based on high school academics, curriculum strength, the application and test scores if provided, at the Admission Committee's discretion.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.75 cumulative Chapman GPA.

name: Dodge College Talent Scholarships (Sodaro-Pankey Talent Scholarship)
value: $2,000 to $5,000 per year for four years while in good academic standing.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No separate application; all Dodge College of Film and Media Arts applicants are considered based on the Creative Supplement in the admission application.
eligibility: First-year applicants to a Dodge College major who show strong creative ability and originality in their application materials. Not available to transfer students.
notes: Renewal requires staying in a Dodge College major, full-time enrollment and a 2.75 cumulative GPA.

name: Fowler Engineering Scholarships
value: $2,000 per year up to 100% of tuition, room and board; available for up to eight semesters.
deadline: Considered if you apply by the admission deadline. Fall 2027: Early Action and Early Decision I November 1, 2026; Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15, 2027.
apply: No separate application; all applicants to a Fowler School of Engineering undergraduate major are considered. Awards appear on the Application Status Page after admission.
eligibility: First-year applicants who apply to a Fowler Engineering major. Merit awards go to students with exemplary academic records.
notes: Fowler awards are given in several categories, some merit-based and some need-based. Renewal requires a STEM major in Fowler, Schmid or Crean, no Fowler course grade below B-, and a 3.0 Chapman GPA.

name: Thurgood Marshall Scholarship
value: Amounts vary; can be as high as $6,000 per year, applied to tuition for fall and spring semesters.
deadline: Offered to select admitted students; no separate scholarship deadline posted. FAFSA due by the March 2 financial aid deadline each year.
apply: No separate application described; select admitted first-generation students are offered the award.
eligibility: Select first-generation students with exceptional academic performance, outstanding community leadership and demonstrated financial need.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.00 cumulative GPA, full-time enrollment and a FAFSA each year.

name: Merit Scholarships
value: $1,000 to full tuition; most are four-year awards.
deadline: December 15 priority consideration for fall applicants (displayed without a year).
apply: No separate application; all admission applicants are automatically considered.
eligibility: All applicants to Hillsdale College; based on the strength of the application with emphasis on academic profile.

name: Leadership Scholarships
value: Amount not stated.
deadline: November 15 for fall-term applicants (displayed without a year).
apply: Submit the admission application, including a resume of extracurricular activities and leadership, by November 15.
eligibility: Fall-term applicants; recognizes involvement in school, church and community.

name: Choral Scholars Scholarship
value: Typically $10,000 per year, renewable according to the terms of the aid agreement.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted; for fall 2026 entry the prescreening video was due December 15, 2025, with on-campus auditions January 30 to 31, 2026.
apply: Submit an unlisted YouTube prescreening video (solo selections, an assigned choral part and vocalises); invited applicants audition on campus.
eligibility: Prospective first-year singers applying for admission to Hillsdale who want to join the Chapel Choir's Choral Scholars program.
notes: Recipients take on choral duties set out in the aid agreement.

name: Honors Scholarship
value: $1,000 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision (Earlham lists November 1 for ED and EA I and December 1 for EA II, fall entry, without a year).
apply: After an Honors Program invitation, submit a 'Teach Us Something in Five Minutes or Less' creative project (article, podcast, video, song, etc.) and present it in person at Scholarship Day.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants admitted to Earlham and invited to the Honors Program. No test score or GPA minimum for selection.
notes: Renewal requires the fall first-year Honors seminar and a 3.4 GPA. International students are eligible, but the award does not reduce the financial contribution required of international applicants.

name: Creative Writing Scholarship
value: $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision (Earlham lists November 1 for ED and EA I and December 1 for EA II, fall entry, without a year).
apply: Submit creative writing work through the scholarship portal; finalists take part in Scholarship Day.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to major or minor in English or creative writing.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA and a creative writing course or a semester as a student editor of The Crucible. International students are eligible, but the award does not reduce the financial contribution required of international applicants.

name: Music Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years. The Rariden Scholarship offers $5,000 per year to select Indiana residents.
deadline: Apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision (Earlham lists November 1 for ED and EA I and December 1 for EA II, fall entry, without a year).
apply: Submit an audition recording (most instruments: two contrasting pieces), a short information sheet and the application form.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to take music classes and/or ensembles; not limited to majors.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA, one ensemble each semester and a lesson every semester. Virtual auditions available. International students are eligible, but the award does not reduce the financial contribution required of international applicants.

name: Art Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision (Earlham lists November 1 for ED and EA I and December 1 for EA II, fall entry, without a year).
apply: Submit a portfolio and the scholarship application form.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to major or minor in art.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA, an art course every semester and an art major or minor. International students are eligible, but the award does not reduce the financial contribution required of international applicants.

name: Theatre Arts Scholarship
value: $1,000 to $2,500 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision (Earlham lists November 1 for ED and EA I and December 1 for EA II, fall entry, without a year).
apply: Submit an audition and the scholarship application form; virtual auditions available.
eligibility: Early Action or Early Decision applicants accepted to the fall class who plan to take theatre classes and/or productions.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.0 GPA plus yearly theatre production and coursework participation. International students are eligible, but the award does not reduce the financial contribution required of international applicants.

name: The Quaker Scholarship
value: Full tuition, housing, and meals, to $5,000, renewable up to four years (as stated).
deadline: Scholarship application due February 1 (no year shown); applicants must also apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision.
apply: Apply by the EA or ED deadline and submit the scholarship application with verification of Quaker meeting membership or Quaker faith.
eligibility: Applicants who are members of a Quaker meeting or can otherwise verify their Quaker faith.

name: Carleton B. Edwards Chemistry Scholarships
value: Starting at $1,000 per year.
deadline: Scholarship application due February 1 (no year shown); applicants must also apply for admission by Early Action or Early Decision.
apply: Apply by the EA or ED deadline and submit the scholarship application with reference letters; chemistry faculty choose recipients.
eligibility: Outstanding incoming students who plan to major in chemistry or biochemistry; judged on high school achievement, interest in chemistry and references.

name: Earlham Science Scholar Program
value: Up to $10,000 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Deadline not stated on the program page.
apply: Submit the online application form and a personal essay on your STEM interest and any independent research.
eligibility: Pell-eligible students entering in the fall who plan to major in biology, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science, data science, earth and environmental science, engineering, mathematics, physics or pre-engineering.
notes: Renewal requires a 2.8 GPA, degree progress and continued financial eligibility.

name: Brooks Scholarship (Music)
value: Four-year, full-tuition scholarship.
deadline: Jan. 15 (displayed without a year).
apply: Upload a music resume, an essay, two recommendation letters (private teacher and a music professional) and either video of two contrasting selections (up to 15 minutes, unedited) or two original compositions to the scholarship portal.
eligibility: High school seniors who will major in music or double major in music and another discipline, with outstanding instrumental/vocal performance or composition and strong academics.
notes: AI-generated scores are not permitted for composers.

name: Bean and FitzGerald Classics Scholarships
value: Full tuition for four years. Two Rev. Henry Bean, S.J. Scholarships each year; a Rev. William FitzGerald, S.J. Scholarship (awarded every four years) is offered this year to a member of the Class of 2031.
deadline: Scholarship application due January 15, 2027; recommender letters due Friday, January 22, 2027.
apply: Submit the Common App plus the classics scholarship application with two essays (600 and 500 words) and one recommender; a short list is interviewed.
eligibility: High school seniors who plan to major in classics. No prior Latin, Greek or Hebrew is required.
notes: The page also says short-list interview requests follow 'January 26, 2026', which appears to be an unupdated date.

name: Ellis Scholarship
value: Full tuition, renewable for all four years.
deadline: Considered with the admission application; finalists interview on campus in February (no year shown).
apply: No separate application; all applicants who live in Worcester are considered. Finalists are invited to interview.
eligibility: Worcester, Massachusetts residents entering their first year at Holy Cross.

name: University Merit Scholarships
value: $10,000 to $30,000, applied to tuition only.
deadline: Considered with the admission application. Posted first-year deadlines (no year shown): Early Action November 1, Early Decision I November 15, Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 15.
apply: No separate application; all admitted students are automatically considered, whether or not they apply for financial aid.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students; based on overall academic record, strength of program and extracurricular involvement. No minimum grades or test scores.

name: The Company Scholars
value: Full cost: tuition, room and board for four years.
deadline: Early Action November 1 or Regular Decision January 15 (no year shown); final selections by April 15.
apply: Submit the Common Application to Fairfield (fee waiver code available); an interview is required.
eligibility: High school seniors at a Cristo Rey Network school or a Jesuit high school who meet Fairfield's academic profile, contribute meaningfully to their community and have significant financial need.
notes: Includes a summer bridge program, faculty mentoring and advising.
